subject: Urgent: Oriole Health v5.1 quant profile swap causing throughput and latency regression
messages:
From: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@oriolehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-17T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Severe degradation after v5.1 deployment - 50% throughput drop, p95 latency climb

Hi Olga / Marissa,

We pushed v5.1 (Redwood recommended quant profile v2.3) to production at 03:00 PT and within ~30 minutes started seeing a major service impact. High level:
- Throughput dropped ~50% for our batch inference pipeline (from ~1.2k TPS to ~600 TPS).
- p95 latency climbed from 180ms to ~720ms for our high-priority route.
- Error rate (5xx and timeouts) increased from ~0.1% to 2.8%.

This hit our peak traffic window and is causing downstream job backpressure. We rolled the change into a canary ring but it looks like rollout propagated to 60% of production. Attached are traces and the pipeline worker logs (orchard_logs_20260917.zip).

Please escalate — our CTO Samir is on the call and wants an immediate mitigation plan. If you need a bridge, we can spin one up right now.

Thanks,
Dana Lopez
Platform Ops, Oriole Health
Attachments: orchard_logs_20260917.zip, p95_report_0917.csv

Immediate asks for your team:
- Can you confirm whether rollback to previous profile (v2.1) is permitted without extra approvals?
- Any specific customer flows we should avoid touching (payment flows, critical jobs)?

We will triage and propose either an emergency rollback or targeted config patch within 30–45 minutes. I will update on the bridge link (if you can spin one, please share).

Olga

-----Internal: Technical triage-----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-17T08:49:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe degradation - preliminary analysis

Olga / team — quick technical summary from our initial runbook checks:
- Symptoms match a kernel-path regression introduced by the quant profile v2.3 for this model family (causes more fallback to the int8 slow path at longer context lengths).
- Repro locally: using Oriole prod input distribution we see ~3x decode step time on the affected sequence length bin (128-256).
- Memory/KV behavior: no OOMs, but cache eviction frequency increased which reduces effective batching.

Attachments: p95_report_0917.csv (aggregated timings), sample trace snippets in orchard_logs_20260917.zip.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Emergency rollback to v2.1 for Oriole production (fastest, will restore previous kernels).
2) Pin route to smaller max_context and lower beam_count as partial mitigation (risk: changes output quality).
3) Deploy a special kernel patch (requires a 2–3 hour engineering window and careful canary).

I recommend option 1 for fastest customer relief. I have a rollback procedure documented (rollback_playbook_v1.md) and can execute once we have signoff.

Marcus
Senior Runtime Engineer

Subject: Re: Severe degradation after v5.1 deployment - rollback suggested

Dana — we recommend an immediate rollback to quant profile v2.1. This has historically restored kernel fast-path behavior for this model family and should bring throughput/latency back within SLO.

We are ready to perform the rollback from our side if you grant permission. Rollback impact: a brief (~2–4 minute) rolling restart on affected nodes, negligible change in model outputs.

If Oriole prefers to initiate, please confirm and share the bridge. If not, we will schedule an emergency window for 09:25 PT.

Olga

- Throughput recovered to ~1.15k TPS within 8 minutes of rolling window.
- p95 latency back near baseline (~200ms).
- Error rate dropped to 0.12%.

- We will add Oriole-specific quant/compat tests into our pre-release canary for model family ORN-xx by next release.

Marissa Cole
